key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Engineering stronger transparent-conductive-oxide/SAM interfaces addresses stress-driven adhesion failure under temperature fluctuations.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer (SAM) formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl density to support multipoint metal–oxygen coordination.
Use cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to reinforce interfacial anchoring.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 cycles between −40 and 85 °C under ISOS-T-3 testing.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish large-area manufacturing compatibility or field durability beyond the reported thermal-cycling test.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
